question: Starvation and diabetes mellitus can lead on to ketoacidosis which of the following features is in our of ketoacidosis due to diabetes mellitus.

options.opa: Increase in glucagon/insulin ratio, increased CAMP and increased blood glucose
options.opb: Decreased insulin, increased free fatty acid which is equivalent to blood glucose
options.opc: Decreased insulin, increased free fatty acid which is not equivalent to blood glucose
options.opd: Elevated insulin and free fatty acid, equivalent to blood glucose

analysis: In the context of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), the primary metabolic disturbances include a significant increase in the glucagon/insulin ratio due to decreased insulin production or action. This imbalance promotes lipolysis, leading to an increase in free fatty acids. These fatty acids are then converted into ketone bodies, contributing to the acidotic state. Additionally, the elevated glucagon/insulin ratio enhances the production of cyclic AMP (cAMP), which further stimulates gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis, thereby increasing blood glucose levels. This sequence of events is well-documented and aligns with the standard biochemical understanding of the pathophysiology of DKA. Option 'opa' correctly encapsulates these processes, stating an increase in the glucagon/insulin ratio, increased cAMP, and increased blood glucose, which are characteristic features of DKA in the setting of diabetes mellitus.
